***
## Key to hydra groups

Modified from Campbell (1987). 

<style>
.tax-key {
  margin-bottom: 1em;
}
.tax-key dt {
  font-weight: bold;
  float: left;
  width: 3.5em;
}
.tax-key dd {
  margin-left: 3.5em;
  margin-bottom: 0.5em;
}
.tax-key .level-2 {
  margin-left: 3.5em;
}
.tax-key .level-3 {
  margin-left: 7em;
}
</style>

<div class="tax-key">
  <dl>
    <dt>1a.</dt>
    <dd>Hydra green due to intracellular algal symbionts;  <br>
    stenotele nematocysts not longer than 11 µm .......................................... <strong>Viridissima group</strong></dd>
    
    <dt>1b.</dt>
    <dd>Hydra not green; stenotele nematocysts longer than 11 µm</dd>
  </dl>

  <dl class="level-2">
    <dt>2a.</dt>
    <dd>Holotrichous isorhiza nematocysts plump (at half as broad as long)</dd>
  </dl>

  <dl class="level-3">
    <dt>3a.</dt>
    <dd>Embryotheca without spines ............................................ <strong>Braueri group</strong></dd> 
    <dt>3b.</dt>
    <dd>Embryotheca with spines ................................................ <strong>Lirosoma group</strong></dd>
  </dl>

  <dl class="level-2">
    <dt>2b.</dt>
    <dd>Holotrichous isorhiza slender, or if plump then embryotheca with spines</dd>
  </dl>

  <dl class="level-3">
    <dt>4a.</dt>
    <dd>Buds acquire 2 lateral tentacles before other tentacles appear;<br> 
    otherwise, stenoteles at least 1.5 times as long as broad <br>
    smooth, spherical embryotheca ...................................... <strong>Oligactis group</strong></dd>
    <dt>4b.</dt>
    <dd>Buds acquire tentacles in some other order; otherwise, <br>
    stenoteles less than 1.5 times as long as broad <br>
    spherical embryotheca with spines.................................... <strong>Vulgaris group</strong></dd>
  </dl>
</div>

---
Campbell, R. D. (1987). A new species of Hydra (Cnidaria: Hydrozoa) from North America with comments on species clusters within the genus. Zoological Journal of the Linnean Society, 91, 253–263.
